relevant_prelims_pyqs.question_text: Consider the following statements: [2021] 1. In India, there is no law restricting candidates from contesting in one Lok Sabha election from three constituencies. 2. In the 1991 Lok Sabha Election, Shri Devi Lal contested from three Lok Sabha constituencies. 3. As per the existing rules, if a candidate contests in one Lok Sabha election from many constituencies, his/her party should bear the cost of bye-elections to the constituencies vacated by him/her in the event of him/her winning in all the constituencies. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
relevant_prelims_pyqs.source_pdf: X-Factor Prelims- Indian Polity for Pre'2027.pdf
relevant_prelims_pyqs.markdown_formatted:
**Q2 (2021)**: Consider the following statements: [2021] 1. In India, there is no law restricting candidates from contesting in one Lok Sabha election from three constituencies. 2. In the 1991 Lok Sabha Election, Shri Devi Lal contested from three Lok Sabha constituencies. 3. As per the existing rules, if a candidate contests in one Lok Sabha election from many constituencies, his/her party should bear the cost of bye-elections to the constituencies vacated by him/her in the event of him/her winning in all the constituencies. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
- (a) 1 only
- (b) 2 only
- (c) 1 and 3
- (d) 2 and 3
- **Answer**: `(b)` ([View Source Page 152](pages/prelims/prelims_page_152.pdf))

relevant_prelims_pyqs.question_text: Consider the following statements: [2020] 1. According to the Constitution of India, a person who is eligible to vote can be made a minister in a State for six months even if he/she is not a member of the Legislature of that State. 2. According to the Representation of People Act, 1951, a person convicted of a criminal offence and sentenced to imprisonment for five years is permanently disqualified from contesting an election even after his release from prison. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
relevant_prelims_pyqs.source_pdf: X-Factor Prelims- Indian Polity for Pre'2027.pdf
relevant_prelims_pyqs.markdown_formatted:
**Q3 (2020)**: Consider the following statements: [2020] 1. According to the Constitution of India, a person who is eligible to vote can be made a minister in a State for six months even if he/she is not a member of the Legislature of that State. 2. According to the Representation of People Act, 1951, a person convicted of a criminal offence and sentenced to imprisonment for five years is permanently disqualified from contesting an election even after his release from prison. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
- (a) 1 only
- (b) 2 only
- (c) Both 1 and 2
- (d) Neither 1 nor 2
- **Answer**: `(d)` ([View Source Page 152](pages/prelims/prelims_page_152.pdf))

relevant_mains_pyqs.question_text: 25, the BJP received 83% of all donations made through Electoral Trusts. 10. Foreign Influence Risks: Retroactive FCRA amendments allow foreign-owned Indian subsidiaries to fund parties, risking national sovereignty. 11. Inadequate Audit Mechanism: Parties choose their own private auditors, leading to potential "friendly audits" and lack of rigor. Way Forward: 1. ECI has suggested that parties should be made to disclose contributions received in cash for smaller sums in case they exceed 20% of total funds raised. 2. Lower Disclosure Threshold: Reduce the anonymous donation limit from ₹20,000 to ₹2,000. 3. Real-time Digital Disclosure: Use the IEMS portal (2026) to mandate uploading of every donation over ₹2,000 within 48 hours. 4. Cap on Party Expenditure: Amend the RPA, 1951 to impose a statutory limit on total party spending (Law Commission 255th Report). 5. Partial State Funding (In-Kind): Provide facilities like fuel, airtime, and paper instead of cash to parties (Indrajit Gupta Committee). 6. National Election Fund: Establish a central pool where corporates donate; the ECI then distributes funds based on vote share. 7. CAG-Approved Audits: Mandate that all political party accounts be audited by a panel of auditors approved by the CAG. 8. Global Best Practice (Germany): Adopt the "Parteienfinanzierung" model where public funds are allocated based on verified vote shares. 9. Re-implement the cap on corporate donations to prevent "shell company" influence. 10. Bring political parties formally under the RTI for all financial and donor-related queries. 11. Enforce Campaign Expenditure Limits a. Monitor actual spending on social media ads, surrogate advertising, influencers etc. b. Link expenditure data to election affidavits and IT returns One Nation One Election ONOE refers to the proposal to synchronize the timing of all elections in India to occur within a single timeframe or cycle. History of ONOE 1. Simultaneous elections were the norm in India for the first four general election cycles (1952, 1957, 1962, and 1967). 2. The cycle was broken due to the premature dissolution of several State Assemblies in 1968 and 1969, followed by the dissolution of the Lok Sabha in 1970 and fresh polls in 1971. 3. The Law Commission (170th Report, 1999) and the Parliamentary Standing Committee (2015) strongly advocated for returning to simultaneous polls to ensure governance stability. Key Benefits of One Nation One Election 1. Reduced Financial Burden for the exchequer - costs of logistics, polling staff, and security. 2. Continuity in Governance: Prevents "policy paralysis" caused by the frequent imposition of the Model Code of Conduct (MCC). 168
